== Book 4 ==

== Biography ==

The Princess is the ruling monarch of the Emerald City, described as the youthful Ruler of Oz who was often lonely for lack of companionship from girls her own age. Her court includes attendants such as her maid Jellia Jamb, and she receives guests within the palace's reception rooms.

When Zeb and the Wizard arrive at the palace, the Princess dines with them alongside Dorothy. During the meal she questions the Wizard about the origin of the name "Oz," asking whether he took his name from the country or whether the country was named after him. She then offers him the position of Official Wizard of her kingdom, an offer he accepts with gratitude, visibly moved at securing such a home.

The Princess keeps close companions in the Lion and the Hungry Tiger, who stand at her side during a footrace between the Sawhorse and the horse Jim. When the Lion moves to stop the animals from fighting after the race, he growls that no one may injure "one of our friends" in the Princess's presence, showing her protective standing among the group.

In a quieter domestic moment during the days of festivity following Dorothy's arrival, the Princess asks Jellia to fetch a white piglet she had left on the dressing-table in her boudoir.

== Narrative role ==

Princess begins life as the ripe Royal Princess growing on the Royal Bush; Dorothy and the Wizard pick her, and upon coming to life she deposes Prince, becoming the new ruler of the Mangaboos. As the new ruler, Princess spares Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard, but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit in the mountain.

== Personality ==

The Princess shows marked curiosity toward strangers she wishes to understand: she is described as "quite curious to meet" the Wizard, and at dinner she presses him directly about whether he named himself after Oz or Oz was named after him. This same directness carries into how she gives instructions to her household, plainly and without harshness, as when she tells her maid, "Please go to my boudoir, Jellia, and get the white piglet I left on the dressing-table."

Her offer to make the Wizard "Official Wizard" of her kingdom, promising he will be "treated with every respect and consideration," reveals a generous and hospitable disposition — a kindness that visibly moves the old man to tears. Yet the same passages suggest a quieter loneliness beneath her rule: she has few girls her own age with whom "it was proper for the Princess to associate," leaving the "youthful Ruler of Oz" often "lonely for lack of companionship," which lends her evident happiness at Dorothy's company particular weight.

== Appearance ==

The Prince of the Mangaboos refers to her as "the girl on the bush," indicating she was still growing among her vegetable people. He states that she must become "fully ripe" before he abandons his sovereignty to her. Examining her, the Wizard judges that she is "quite sure she's ripe," fit to be picked as the Royal Princess.

== Powers ==

According to the Prince of the Mangaboos, the Princess is not born in the ordinary way: she is described as a Royal Princess who must become "fully ripe" before assuming rule, at which point the Prince states he will abandon his own sovereignty to her. The Wizard, examining her, judged her "ripe" and proposed picking her so that she could come to life and take up her place as Ruler.

== Trivia ==

* Despite being addressed throughout as "Princess," she reveals her own name to the Wizard, stating, "my own name is Ozma."
* She keeps a pet white piglet on the dressing-table in her private boudoir, entrusted to the care of her maid Jellia.
* The Lion and the Hungry Tiger position themselves at her side in a show of protection, the Lion declaring that no one may injure their friends in her presence.

== Book 5 ==

== Biography ==

The Princess is addressed as "your Highness" and referred to as the "girl Ruler" of Oz. She hosts a birthday party to which Dorothy is a guest, and greets Dorothy with warmth when Dorothy arrives, prompting Dorothy to hug and kiss her. The Princess asks Dorothy who she imagines mixed up the roads that started Dorothy wandering toward Oz, suggesting she herself had a hand in the matter, though she answers Dorothy's question about this only with "Didn't I?" — leaving her own role deliberately unconfirmed.

When Dorothy presents the shaggy man at the throne, calling him "my friend, the shaggy man, who owns the Love Magnet," the Princess receives him graciously, telling him he is welcome to Oz. Her manner throughout is described as gracious, and she is shown ruling from a throne within her palace.

== Relationships ==

'''[[King Bud of Noland]]''' — a family tie is suggested by the records, though the passage describing a sibling bond names the Princess Fluff as King Bud's sister rather than this Princess, so the connection may not concern her at all.

'''[[Dorothy]]''' — friend. The two speak directly at the birthday gathering, with the Princess questioning Dorothy about who had mixed up the roads toward Oz.

'''[[Johnny Dooit]]''' — an acquaintance is suggested by a record of him thanking the Princess for her hospitality, though this exchange does not appear directly among the passages here.

'''[[THE shaggy man]]''' — acquaintance. She receives him graciously at her throne after Dorothy presents him, telling him he is welcome to Oz.

'''[[Wizard]]''' — an acquaintance is suggested by the records, though no direct exchange between them appears in the accounts here.

<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Book 6 ==

== Biography ==

The Princess is addressed by this title in scenes tied to Ozma's court and to Dorothy's status within Oz. Ozma is shown possessing a Magic Picture that lets her view any part of the world she wishes and watch anyone she is interested in; through it she once observed Dorothy in her Kansas home, and on another occasion she used it daily to inspect the progress of a tunnel being dug, a task she considered her duty even though it was not especially interesting to her. Ozma is directly addressed as "Princess" by her companions, including a remark from the Shaggy Man agreeing that reforming the wicked people mattered more than saving Oz.

The title is also applied to Dorothy, who dressed in her prettiest gown and put on her coronet before a dinner with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and Jack Pumpkinhead, thinking it might be the last time she would appear as a Princess of Oz. Separately, a rabbit wearing a monocle addressed Dorothy as "Princess" while informing her that her companions could not enter Bunnybury with her.
